name: fdp-table
title: Fraction, decimal & percentage table
tagline: Fraction–decimal–percentage equivalence table; write one form per row and the other two derive string-exact (recurring dots); cells occlude and rows sort by value.
description: An equivalence table whose rows are numbers and whose columns are the Fraction, Decimal and Percentage forms of each. Every row writes exactly one form; the other two cells are computed string-exact — fractions reduce, decimals come from exact long division with recurring-digit dots (one third → 0.3̇, one sixth → 0.16̇), percentages are the value × 100 with a "%". Cells occlude to "?" (complete the table), blank for staged fills, or amber for the answer; an order:"ascending"|"descending" mode sorts the rows by their exact value (ties — 0.3 and 30% are equal — sit together). Use it to complete an FDP table, convert one value between forms, order or compare a mixed list, or drill the equivalences. percentage-square shows one percentage on a hundred-grid and fraction-shape shades a single shape — this is the multi-row equivalence grid neither draws.
whenToUse: Reach for this whenever fractions, decimals and percentages are taught as the same number in three forms: complete-the-table (give one column, find the others), convert a single value between forms, order a mixed list of fractions/decimals/percentages, compare two values, or recall the common equivalences (1/2, 1/4, 3/4, 1/5, 1/10, 1/3, 1/8 …). Author each row with exactly one of fraction / decimal / percent; the rest is computed — you never write a conversion. Common configurations: complete the table — occludeDerived: true turns every non-authored cell into "?", so a column of authored fractions becomes a fill-in decimal and percentage grid; convert one value — a single row with occlude on the target column (and columns to drop the form you do not want); order a list — give each number in its own form, set order: "ascending" (rows sort by value), and show the Decimal column as the common comparison form; compare — two rows + order. Recurring values (thirds, sixths, ninths, sevenths) must be authored as the fraction, never as a truncated decimal — the engine renders the recurring decimal with the dot. Keep the same columns across the blocks of one lesson so pupils track one layout. Staged builds: open on the authored forms with the rest occluded or blank, reveal the conversions, then bring order in last — the base (authored column, others "?") stands alone as a sensible "complete this" figure. Synonyms teachers use: FDP, fractions decimals percentages, equivalent, convert, ordering FDP, comparing fractions and decimals, percentage of, recurring decimal.

items.description: One number, shown across the equivalence columns. Author EXACTLY ONE of fraction / decimal / percent — that is the given form; the other two cells are derived. occlude / blank / highlight name which columns of THIS row are hidden, emptied or emphasised.

fraction.description: Give this row as a fraction num/den. Shown in the Fraction column AS WRITTEN (6/8 stays 6/8 — author 3/4 if you want it reduced); the derived Decimal and Percentage use its exact value. den must be ≥ 1.

num.description: Numerator (top). May be 0; negative is allowed but FDP work is normally non-negative.

den.description: Denominator (bottom), a positive integer. den 1 renders as the whole number.

decimal.description: Give this row as a decimal, e.g. 0.35 (→ 7/20, 35%) or 1.5 (→ 3/2, 150%). Author a TERMINATING decimal only: a recurring value like one third must be authored as the fraction 1/3, not a truncated 0.333 (which is exactly 333/1000).

percent.description: Give this row as a percentage, e.g. 35 means 35% (→ 7/20, 0.35); 12.5 means 12.5% (→ 1/8, 0.125). May exceed 100 (150 → 3/2). For a recurring percentage (one third → 33.3̇%) author the fraction instead.

occlude.description: Columns of this row to render as "?" — the question hook ("what goes here?"). The cell stays in place; its value appears NOWHERE (anti-leak). Use to hide the cells a pupil must work out.

blank.description: Columns of this row to render EMPTY (nothing at all) — for a staged build that fills cells in one stage at a time. Different from occlude: "?" poses a question, blank poses nothing yet. blank wins over occlude.

highlight.description: Columns of this row to amber (light fill + bold border, amber text) — the answer or the cell to draw the eye to.

rows.description: The numbers in the table, one per row, top to bottom. Each row authors exactly one form (fraction / decimal / percent); the other columns derive. When order is set the rows are sorted by value, so author order only matters as the un-sorted "question" arrangement.

columns.description: Which equivalence columns to show, in this left-to-right order. Default ["fraction","decimal","percent"]. Drop one for a two-column lesson (e.g. ["fraction","decimal"] for fraction↔decimal only). A row may author a form whose column is hidden — its value still feeds the others.

order.description: Sort the rows by their exact value — "ascending" smallest first, "descending" largest first. This is the ordering answer: give the mixed list, set order, and the rows rearrange. Equal values (0.3 and 30%) keep their authored order, sitting together. Omit to keep the authored row order (the un-ordered question).

occludeDerived.description: Render every DERIVED (non-authored) cell as "?" in one go — the "complete the table" answer space. A row that authored its fraction shows the fraction and hides the decimal and percentage. Per-row occlude still adds more. Default false.

blankDerived.description: Render every DERIVED (non-authored) cell EMPTY (nothing) — a blank answer space or the base of a staged "fill it in" build. Like occludeDerived but with no "?". blank wins over "?". Default false.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the table; the top padding grows to clear it.

caption.description: Optional italic line below the table, e.g. a short context note. Clears the table by a full line-height. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.

examples.label: Worked example — common equivalences (1/2, 1/4, 3/4, 1/5) in all three forms
Complete the table (occluded question) — given the fractions, find decimal and percentage
Blank answer space — mixed given forms, the rest empty to fill in
Convert one value — write 7/8 as a decimal and a percentage (target cells amber)
Order a mixed list (ascending) — fractions, decimals and percentages sorted by value

params.caption: Converting each to a decimal makes the order clear.

examples.label: Hard case — order ⅓, 0.3, 30%, 0.35 (a recurring decimal and an equal pair)

params.caption: Watch the recurring decimal — and notice two of these are equal.
